The zlib format (RFC 1950) wraps a deflate stream (RFC 1951) in a two-byte
header and the Adler-32 checksum of the uncompressed data. The Compression
Streams standard calls it "deflate", and the raw deflate stream without the
header and the checksum "deflate-raw". The gzip format (RFC 1952) wraps the
same deflate stream in a longer header, which may hold a file name, a
comment and a modification time, and in a trailer that holds the CRC-32 and
the size of the uncompressed data, modulo 2^32.

Node.js writes this file's zlib stream with the zlib library that it bundles,
whose encoder chooses its blocks and matches differently from zlib-rs. The
decoder must accept any valid stream, not only the streams that its own
encoder writes, so the test decodes a stream that another encoder wrote.

1. A stream that ends before its final block is truncated.
2. A stream whose checksum does not match its data is corrupt.
3. Data after the end of the stream is corrupt, except another gzip member.
4. Output beyond the limit fails before the decoder writes it.
